facts.content: Patient has a 3-day history of diarrhea with central abdominal pain and vomiting.
facts.source_text: CC: 3-day hx diarrhea with central abdominal pain and vomiting

facts.content: Patient has had watery diarrhea for 3 days, unchanged, with urgency and tenesmus.
facts.source_text: Watery diarrhea x3 days; unchanged; urgency/tenesmus; needs proximity to toilet; no hematochezia

facts.content: Patient experiences periumbilical and infra-umbilical abdominal pain that improves after a bowel movement.
facts.source_text: Abd pain: periumbilical/infra-umbilical, improves after BM; mild TTP on self-press

facts.content: Patient vomited this morning after eating fruit, experiences intermittent nausea.
facts.source_text: Vomited this morning after fruit; no hematemesis (red color thought to be strawberries); intermittent nausea

facts.content: Patient reports reduced oral intake and possibly low fluids.
facts.source_text: PO intake reduced; possibly low fluids

facts.content: Patient reports no chest pain and baseline asthma-related shortness of breath, able to walk and talk but limited by toilet needs.
facts.source_text: No chest pain; baseline asthma-related SOB only; able to walk/talk limited by toilet needs

facts.content: Patient reports no clear fever but has been sweating over the last 4 days, unsure about temperature.
facts.source_text: No clear fever; reports sweating over 4 days; unsure about temp

facts.content: Patient is concerned that a recent inhaler switch may contribute to symptoms, clinician advised unlikely.
facts.source_text: Possible food-related; concerned inhaler switch may contribute (clinician advised unlikely)

facts.content: Patient has a history of asthma.
facts.source_text: PMH: Asthma

facts.content: Patient uses an inhaler, brand changed recently.
facts.source_text: Meds: Inhaler (brand changed recently; details not provided)

facts.content: Patient reports no known drug allergies.
facts.source_text: Allergies: NKDA (per pt)

facts.content: Patient's father died of bowel cancer approximately 10 years ago.
facts.source_text: FH: Father died of bowel cancer ~10 yrs ago

facts.content: Patient's work is impacted due to frequent toilet use, staying home.
facts.source_text: SH: Work impacted due to frequent toilet use; staying home

facts.content: Patient self-reports mild abdominal tenderness with palpation.
facts.source_text: Self-reported mild abdominal tenderness with palpation

facts.content: Impression of acute gastroenteritis with dehydration risk.
facts.source_text: Acute gastroenteritis with dehydration risk — 3 days non-bloody diarrhea, periumbilical cramps relieved by BM, single emesis episode, reduced intake; afebrile by history but uncertain.

facts.content: Asthma is stable, patient is using an inhaler.
facts.source_text: Asthma — stable; using inhaler; recent brand change.

facts.content: Family history of colorectal cancer, but current presentation is more consistent with infectious gastroenteritis.
facts.source_text: FHx colorectal cancer — pt anxious; current presentation more c/w infectious gastroenteritis.

facts.content: Encourage oral rehydration solutions with frequent small sips and avoid caffeine or alcohol.
facts.source_text: Hydration: Encourage oral rehydration solutions; frequent small sips; avoid caffeine/alcohol.

facts.content: Advised BRAT-style or light diet as tolerated, advance as symptoms improve, avoid dairy, high-fat, or spicy foods short term.
facts.source_text: Diet: BRAT-style/light diet as tolerated; advance as symptoms improve; avoid dairy/high-fat/spicy foods short term.

facts.content: Consider oral antiemetic if nausea returns, avoid antimotility agents if fever or bloody stool develops.
facts.source_text: Symptomatic: Consider oral antiemetic if nausea recurs; avoid antimotility agents if fever/bloody stool develops; otherwise short course loperamide acceptable if no red flags.

facts.content: Seek in-person evaluation for persistent symptoms, high fever, severe abdominal pain, signs of dehydration, or bloody stool/emesis.
facts.source_text: Monitoring/red flags: Seek in-person eval if persistent symptoms >48–72 hrs, high fever, severe/worsening abd pain, signs of dehydration (dizziness, oliguria), bloody stool/emesis, or inability to tolerate PO.

facts.content: Stay home until improving and diarrhea-free for 48 hours before returning to work.
facts.source_text: Work/Isolation: Stay home until improving and 48 hrs diarrhea-free for work return.

facts.content: Continue usual inhaler as inhaler change is unlikely cause of current symptoms.
facts.source_text: Asthma: Continue usual inhaler; inhaler change unlikely cause; monitor usual control.

facts.content: If not improving in 1-2 days, book in-person GP for exam and discuss CRC risk and screening separately once acute illness resolves.
facts.source_text: Follow-up: If not improving in 1–2 days, book in-person GP for exam; discuss CRC risk and screening separately once acute illness resolves.
